mappings.note: Resources usable without modification -- the natural/human-made division, which is what C-SST1.1-LO-1 asks the student to analyse. Not LO-2: nothing about judicious use is tested.
Machinery and vehicles as human-made resources. The same classification, from the other side.
A principle of sustainable development, which is the justification for judicious use in C-SST1.1-LO-2. This is what separates it from the classification items.
How to conserve resources -- judicious use stated directly.
Defines sustainable development, the concept C-SST1.1-LO-2 rests on.
An example of human resources. Classification of resource type, so LO-1.
Non-renewable examples. Type, not use.
Human-made examples. Type, not use.
Natural substances changed in form become human-made resources -- the boundary between the two categories LO-1 names.
Stock: how much of a resource is available. A quantity question about distribution, which is LO-1's subject.
Why a substance becomes a resource at all -- its value. The prior question to any classification, so LO-1.
Which resources carry most economic value. Still classification, not conservation.
Patent -- exclusive rights over an invention, a human-made resource. LO-1 covers human-made resources; no judgement about their use is asked.
Resources taking millions of years to renew: the non-renewable category.
Processed food as a human-made resource.
The number and ability of people -- human resources, a category under LO-1.
Tropical forests as a natural, renewable resource.
Asks which option is NOT sustainable development, so the student must hold the principle of judicious use and test cases against it -- LO-2.
Renewable examples. Type.
Improving the quality of human lives is one of the stated aims of sustainable development, so LO-2 rather than classification.
What turns a substance into a resource -- technology and value. Companion to qid:110099.
Using resources carefully and allowing them time to renew: conservation, which is LO-2's judicious use.
Resources created by human beings. Type.
Defines value, the property that makes something a resource at all.
